group.passage: In glittering dance costumes and with a boy band face, he glides with such grace that even the sports commentators are at a loss for words. Then, with the final note of music, plushies of Winnie and teddies or bouquets rain down on the rink. Only one skater in the world has this charm—Yuzuru Hanyu, the “Ice Prince.” Hanyu started skating at the tender age of four as a therapy for his asthma problems. His teacher spotted his talent when the prodigy spent only one day learning to do spins that took others three months. In 2011, the 311 earthquake destroyed the skating rink where he was practicing. A truck driver timely saved him and gave him Winnie tissue box, which becomes his lucky charm. Eleven years later, in 2022, the 27-year-old skating star has bagged two Olympic golds, broken 19 world records, and donated over $300,000 U.S. dollars to his tsunami-struck hometown. Even one skating anime “Yuri!!! on ICE” is generally believed to build the character prototype around Hanyu. No other skaters have caused such a sensation. So what is special about this heartthrob? While other winning skaters may only be good at pulling off all the stunts, this whiz composes his music, renders each piece his unique interpretation, and delivers all the techniques with emotions. In “Parisienne Walkways,” he personified Michael Jackson on the ice by snapping his head to the beat, and weaving the quadruple jumps seamlessly into his fluid turns. In “Spring, Coming,” he spun like a cherry blossom, landed like a graceful dandelion, and kissed the ice like sipping the honeydew. Watching him skate simply absorbs everyone into the fantasy world he creates. With the delicate combination of musicality, the jaw-dropping techniques and expressive postures, he has elevated the sport of skating to a whole new artistic height. As World and Olympic figure skating coach Carol Lane put it, “There are good skaters, there are great skaters, and then there is Yuzuru Hanyu.”
